t: A tiny two-channel software defined radio card that slips into a laptop slot.
steps: Order the xSDR from Crowd Supply or Mouser. Add the M.2 to PCIe breakout with SMA cables or a USB-C adapter.
Get an antenna for the band you want, such as an FM or 1090 MHz antenna.
Put the card in the adapter and connect an antenna to a receive port.
Install the usdr-lib host library and SoapySDR on a Linux computer.
Install SDR++ and pick the xSDR as the source.
Tune to a local FM station and watch the waterfall display.
Move on to GNU Radio examples next.
meta: Open Board. From $549. A few stores.
